# Business-Day Rule for Registration Date — Findings

This is the **Spring PetClinic REST** project, built with **Maven** (`/home/daniel/sandbox/pom.xml`, artifact `spring-petclinic-rest`, packaged via `spring-boot-starter-parent`). It uses the OfficeFloor (`net.officefloor`) "WoOF" function-injection style, so the create-owner pipeline is split into small `service(...)` functions.

## 1. Main implementation — the business-day adjustment

**`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/BusinessDays.java`**

This is the single source of truth. Package-private final utility, one static method:

```java
17  /** Roll a weekend date forward to the next Monday; return a weekday unchanged. */
18  static LocalDate rollForward(LocalDate date) {
19      LocalDate rolled = date;
20      while (rolled.getDayOfWeek() == DayOfWeek.SATURDAY
21              || rolled.getDayOfWeek() == DayOfWeek.SUNDAY) {
22          rolled = rolled.plusDays(1);
23      }
24      return rolled;
25  }
```

**How it works today:** pure weekend skipping. It loops, adding one day at a time, while the day is Saturday or Sunday, so a Saturday/Sunday rolls forward to the following Monday; a weekday is returned unchanged. **There is NO holiday handling in the production code** — only weekends are skipped.

**Callers (two, both in the create-owner flow):**

- **`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/BuildOwner.java`** (line 30). Computes the "effective" registration date — the supplied `registrationDate` or, if null, `LocalDate.now()` (line 19-22). A supplied *future* date is rejected first with `FutureRegistrationDateException` (400) at line 25-26. Then it stores the adjusted date: `owner.setRegistrationDate(BusinessDays.rollForward(effective));` (line 30). This is the value that flows into downstream derivations (membership number year, tenure, etc.).

- **`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/EnsureDailyOwnerLimit.java`** (line 28). Recomputes the same adjusted business day (`effective` defaulted to `now()`, then `BusinessDays.rollForward`) to count existing owners for that day and enforce the daily create limit (429 via `DailyOwnerLimitException`). It deliberately mirrors `BuildOwner` so the count key matches what gets stored.

Note also **`FlagBulkSignup.java`** (line 23) compares against the already-adjusted `registrationDate` stored on the entity (it does not call `rollForward` itself; it relies on `BuildOwner` having adjusted it).

## 2. Existing tests for the business-day rule

Only one test project exists, under `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/` (black-box acceptance tests, JUnit 5).

**`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceTest.java`** — the only assertion directly on this rule:

```java
9   /** holiday-business-day: the default registration date rolls past public holidays as well as
10   * weekends. ... assert the invariant ...: the default registrationDate is never a Saturday or Sunday. */
14  @Test
15  void coreDefaultDateIsBusinessDay() throws Exception {
16      DayOfWeek dow = LocalDate.parse(
17          fetchOwner(createOwnerOk(structuredOwner())).get("registrationDate").asText()).getDayOfWeek();
18      assertTrue(dow != DayOfWeek.SATURDAY && dow != DayOfWeek.SUNDAY, dow.toString());
19  }
```

It creates an owner (no registrationDate supplied → server default), fetches it back, and asserts the returned `registrationDate` is not a weekend. It only checks the weekend invariant, not holidays.

There is **no dedicated unit test for `BusinessDays.rollForward`** — the method is only exercised end-to-end via this acceptance test.

## 3. Holiday references

Holidays are referenced **only in tests and doc comments — never in production code**.

**`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceBase.java`**:

```java
239  /** Fixed public holidays the business-day roll skips (year of the run). */
240  protected static final Set<LocalDate> HOLIDAYS = Set.of(
241      LocalDate.parse("2026-01-01"), LocalDate.parse("2026-01-26"),
242      LocalDate.parse("2026-04-25"), LocalDate.parse("2026-12-25"), LocalDate.parse("2026-12-28"));
...
267  /** Roll a date forward over weekends and pinned holidays to the next business day. */
268  protected LocalDate toBusinessDay(LocalDate d) {
269      while (d.getDayOfWeek() == DayOfWeek.SATURDAY || d.getDayOfWeek() == DayOfWeek.SUNDAY
270              || HOLIDAYS.contains(d)) {
271          d = d.plusDays(1);
272      }
273      return d;
274  }
```

Important mismatch worth flagging: this test helper `toBusinessDay` **does** skip holidays, but (a) the production `BusinessDays.rollForward` does **not** skip holidays, and (b) `toBusinessDay` is currently **dead code** — it is defined but never called by any test assertion (verified by grep across `src/`; only its definition line matches). The `AcceptanceTest` doc comment (lines 9-11) explicitly notes that the holiday calendar/server clock "can't be driven black-box," which is why the actual test only asserts the weaker weekend invariant.

Other holiday mentions are just comments: `AcceptanceBase.java:223` (pinned reference-data comment) and the `BusinessDays.java`/`EnsureDailyOwnerLimit.java` javadoc describing weekend roll-forward.

## Build system & running the tests

- **Build system: Maven.** Root `/home/daniel/sandbox/pom.xml`; wrapper `/home/daniel/sandbox/mvnw` (and `mvnw.cmd`). Parent is `spring-boot-starter-parent`.
- No custom surefire/failsafe configuration exists in the pom (grep found none), so standard Spring Boot defaults apply. The acceptance tests are named `*Test` and use JUnit 5 (`spring-boot-starter-test`, `woof_test`), so they run under the normal **unit-test (surefire)** phase.
- Some classes (OpenAPI DTOs such as `OwnerFieldsDto`) are **generated at build time**, so a plain compile/build is required before/with testing (readme.md lines 195-218).

Commands (from repo root):
- Run the whole suite: `./mvnw test`
- Full build incl. code generation + tests: `./mvnw clean install` (readme.md:218)
- Single test: `./mvnw test -Dtest=AcceptanceTest`
- Run the app: `./mvnw spring-boot:run` (readme.md:25)

## Summary of current behavior
The registration-date business-day rule lives entirely in `BusinessDays.rollForward` and adjusts **weekends only** (Sat/Sun → next Monday) by incrementing one day at a time. It is applied in `BuildOwner` (persisted value) and re-derived in `EnsureDailyOwnerLimit` (daily-limit key). Holiday awareness exists **only** in the test base class (`HOLIDAYS` set + unused `toBusinessDay` helper) and in comments/spec intent — the production code does not skip holidays, and the one live test only asserts the weekend invariant.

The build passes. Here's a summary of the change.

## What I did

Extended the registration-date business-day rule in `BusinessDays.rollForward` so an adjusted date landing on a listed public holiday rolls forward to the next non-holiday business day (previously it only skipped weekends).

**`BusinessDays.java`** (`src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/`):
- Added the fixed holiday calendar as a `Set<LocalDate>`: `2026-01-01, 2026-01-26, 2026-04-25, 2026-12-25, 2026-12-28`.
- Changed the roll-forward loop condition from "is weekend" to "is weekend **or** is holiday", so it keeps stepping one day at a time — correctly handling chains where a holiday abuts a weekend (e.g. Fri 2026-12-25 → skips Sat/Sun → Mon 2026-12-28 is also a holiday → Tue 2026-12-29).

Because both call sites — `BuildOwner` (the persisted date) and `EnsureDailyOwnerLimit` (the daily-limit key) — go through this one method, both stay consistent. I also updated the now-stale doc comments in all three files.

The holiday list I used matches the `HOLIDAYS` set already pinned in the test base class (`AcceptanceBase.java`) exactly.

## Tests

`./mvnw -o test` → **BUILD SUCCESS**, `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0`. The acceptance test `coreDefaultDateIsBusinessDay` (which asserts the default registration date is never a weekend) passes.

One note: the specification's holiday behavior can't be driven black-box (it depends on the server clock and the fixed 2026 calendar), so there's no live test that lands a create on a specific holiday — the existing acceptance test only asserts the weekend invariant, as its own comment explains. The implementation nonetheless fully satisfies the specified rule.
